_comment: Differences from the published 1.5.5 that the OWNER has accepted, each with a rationale and a kind:
improvement  additive or strictly better; a 1.5.5 client/operator keeps working unchanged
A matching cell reports as ACCEPTED in its own column — never as a silent pass — so a later change
to the same surface still shows. `cells` are id regexes; `classes` limits the acceptance to those
divergence classes (a status or usage change on an 'improvement' entry is still red).
Zero UNACCEPTED divergences is the ship gate.

An entry with `transform: {candidate: [[regex, replacement], ...]}` is line-precise: the candidate's stderr/body text is rewritten before the diff, so only that token is forgiven; the cell reports ACCEPTED, never PASS.
breaking     a deliberate change named in the 1.6.0 CHANGELOG (`changelog` field required) — the ONLY kind that may accept a `status` or `effects.usage` class
The differ refuses any entry that accepts `status` or `effects.usage` without kind=breaking and a `changelog` field, and any entry with neither `cells` nor `classes` (a total blanket).

EVERY entry, improvement or breaking, owes a `changelog` line that appears verbatim in CHANGELOG.md (ARCHITECTURE.md's owner rule accepts an improvement 'named in the CHANGELOG' too), or an explicit `"changelog": null` with a `changelog_reason`; a breaking entry may never waive. scripts/changelog-register-check.sh is the gate.

accepted.id: D-1 diagnostic codes
accepted.changelog: Every error and warning line carries a diagnostic code.
accepted.rationale: SCOPE (added 2026-09-06, shadow-oracle round-5): this entry carried no `cells`, so it defaulted to `.` and ran over all 2299 cells -- and a fired transform used to hand the cell's whole raw class list to the accepted column, so any cell where this rewrite happened to fire could have a `status` forgiven by it. The lines it rewrites live in a process's stderr or its stdout, which only the exec- and script-driven cells have; the scope is those families and nothing else. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: 1.6.0 prefixes every [error]/[warn]/warning: stderr line with a diagnostic code (BUSBAR-NNNN:) and every boot log line with diag=BUSBAR-NNNN; the text after the code is byte-identical to 1.5.5. SCOPE COUNT 461 -> 462 (2026-09-07): the new boot.refusal|BOOT-152b|boot cell — the boot-mode twin of BOOT-152, which records the provider-credential refusal that replaced the 1.5.5 degrade (register entry F-016) — is an exec-driven boot cell, so it falls inside this family scope like every other one. The transform's REACH is unchanged; one more cell exists for it to reach.

accepted.id: D-2 jemalloc line is info
accepted.changelog: The jemalloc background-purge line is `[info]` on macOS
accepted.rationale: SCOPE (added 2026-09-06, shadow-oracle round-5): same as D-1 -- no `cells` meant the whole corpus. The jemalloc line is a BOOT LOG line, so it can only appear on a cell that runs the binary: the exec- and script-driven families. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: On macOS the jemalloc background-thread line is [info] with an explanation instead of 1.5.5's [warn]; same fallback behaviour. SCOPE COUNT 461 -> 462 (2026-09-07): the new boot.refusal|BOOT-152b|boot cell — the boot-mode twin of BOOT-152, which records the provider-credential refusal that replaced the 1.5.5 degrade (register entry F-016) — is an exec-driven boot cell, so it falls inside this family scope like every other one. The transform's REACH is unchanged; one more cell exists for it to reach.

candidate: ^\[info\] jemalloc background purge thread unavailable on this target \((.*?)\) — EXPECTED on macOS, which has no background-thread mallctl; busbar's idle-purge fallback keeps RSS returning to idle after a load burst$
[warn] could not enable jemalloc background purge thread (\1); enabling busbar's idle purge fallback so RSS still returns to idle after a load burst

accepted.changelog: One new `/metrics` series on a 1.5.5 config:
accepted.rationale: One additive /metrics series on a 1.5.5 config: busbar_metering_pending_coalesced_total (write-behind overflow sentinel). No 1.5.5 series changed.

accepted.id: F-011 additive admin views
accepted.changelog: Admin views gained fields; none changed.
accepted.rationale: Hook views gain fires_at/groups/phase; the overlay-section 404 lists the new sections; openapi.json adds the mcp/a2a endpoints. Every 1.5.5 field is unchanged. SPLIT 2026-09-05 (round-3 audit): effects.readback moved out of this improvement entry into F-011r. effects.readback is now a MONEY class (diff-cells.py rates it 10: it is the proof that the write the cell made actually persisted, and as what), and the readback half is not purely additive — the hook view's always-null `at` field is REMOVED in favour of fires_at, which is a declared breaking change and needs a changelog line. KIND MOVED improvement -> additive 2026-09-08 (busbar-oracle v0.3.3): the owner ruled on 2026-09-07 that key-list and view GROWTH is a new feature and not a break, and `additive` is the kind that makes that ruling checkable — the tool now PROVES the candidate a JSON superset of the golden at every path the golden names before it forgives `body`/`headers`, so this entry can no longer forgive a 1.5.5 field that changed value or went away. DESCRIPTION_CORRECTIONS ADDED 2026-09-11 (keep-oracle-base-reds): admin.ops|DeleteOverlaySection|not-found's `/error/message` string leaf was still standing RED — the overlay-section list growing from four names to eight (commit ee4486486, the plane-extraction squash that generalized `OverlaySection::all()` over `NamedMapSection::sections()`) also reworded the sentence's lead-in from 1.5.5's "expected `a`, `b`, ... or `d`" to "expected one of ..." (the SAME convention 1.5.5's own serde-derived unknown-field messages already use elsewhere in this codebase, e.g. `config::augment_config_error`'s "expected one of `chain`"), so the leaf is not a byte-for-byte list-growth splice and `text_list_growth` cannot prove it. The count growing from four sections to eight is the exact, intended, CHANGELOG-named growth this entry already claims ("the overlay-section 404 lists the sections that now exist"); the wording-convention move onto "expected one of" is the same one every other unknown-key message in this tree already uses. Registered as a correction rather than reverted: reverting would put this ONE message back on the only `a, b, or c` phrasing template left in the tree.

accepted.id: F-011r hook write readback: `at` gives way to `fires_at`
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 parity triage; split out 2026-09-05 (round-3 audit)
accepted.rationale: The follow-up GET a hook write's cell performs reads the same hook view the GET cells read: it gains fires_at/groups/phase and LOSES the always-null `at` field. The additive half is F-011's; the removal is a declared 1.6.0 break named in the CHANGELOG's rewritten-spellings paragraph, so the readback class it moves is registered here as kind=breaking rather than folded into an improvement. Scoped to exactly the four cells that HAVE an effects.readback in the golden (admin.ops|PostHooks|ok, |PutHooksName|ok, |PatchHooksNameSettings|ok, |DeleteHooksName|ok); admin.ops|PostHooks|if-match-stale and every hooks|* cell record no readback at all. The readback's status and path are unchanged in all four — only the view's field set moves.
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Changed: the always-null `at` field on the hook view gives way to `fires_at` (rewritten for you by --migrate-config)

accepted.id: F-013 validation wording
accepted.changelog: Validation messages know the new keys.
accepted.rationale: The new token limit metrics appear in a limit's expected-one-of list; reserved-name / credential-mode sentences rephrased. Same refusal, same exit code. NARROWED 2026-09-05 (the plane-key-lift fix): the top-level plane-key row dropped — the TOP-LEVEL expected-one-of list no longer includes the plane keys, because the 1.6.0-additive keys are lifted off the document before the frozen 1.5.5-shaped parse. That cell is byte-identical to 1.5.5 now and needs no acceptance. NARROWED AGAIN 2026-09-06 (oracle-phase0, committed-golden triage) for the two cells this entry should never have carried. BOOT-020: the divergence it forgave was 'protocol list reordered', and a reorder of an operator-visible list is neither additive nor better — it is a change nobody announced. The PUBLISHED 1.5.5 binary prints `anthropic, openai, gemini, bedrock, responses, cohere`; the plugin consolidation had moved it to `anthropic, gemini, openai, …` believing that was already the shipped order. The order is RESTORED in `busbar_llm_codec::DECLS`, so BOOT-020 is byte-identical to 1.5.5 again and owes no acceptance at all. BOOT-043b: the unknown-member refusal did not merely rephrase a sentence — its FRAME LINE moved from the validate stage to the resolve stage, which an operator's log match sees; it is registered on its own terms as kind=breaking (F-013b) rather than folded into an improvement. NARROWED AGAIN 2026-09-07, and this time by FIXING rather than re-scoping. Three of the five cells this entry named were forgiven for wording that was never worth changing, so the wording was changed back and the cells left this register: BOOT-043b's refusal is returned to the VALIDATE stage (`config::resolve`'s pool-kind inference no longer refuses a member it cannot resolve — it decides a plane, and a name that resolves nowhere decides nothing — so `config_validate` refuses it in 1.5.5's words under the `config validation failed:` frame; the member still cannot escape, because a pool that takes no plane stays on the LLM lane where that validator runs, and one that takes a plane from its other members is refused by `check_failover_pool` against that plane's registry). F-013b, which registered that stage move as a break, IS DELETED along with its CHANGELOG line, because there is no longer a difference to accept. BOOT-P07 and BOOT-P09 were pure rephrasings of the reserved-name and credential-mode sentences by the three-plane `split_section` template; both are restored to 1.5.5 byte-for-byte with the section/noun substituted in, pinned by `assert_eq!` tests, and dropped from the `cells` regex. WHAT REMAINS IS THE ONE REAL DIFFERENCE: BOOT-P20/P29/P30 name the four new token-limit metric keys (`tokens_input`, `tokens_output`, `tokens_cache_read`, `tokens_cache_write`) in a limit's expected-one-of lists. Those keys EXIST in 1.6.0's limit grammar, so hiding them from the list an operator is told to choose from would be a message that lies about what the binary accepts — a worse defect than the divergence. The owner is deciding whether that is an improvement to keep or a break to register on its own terms; `kind` is left at improvement in the meantime, unchanged, so nothing is silently reclassified while the decision is open. COUNT FOLLOWS THE NARROWING: `expected_cells` is 3, one per BOOT-P id this entry still names — not the 5 it forgave before BOOT-043b, BOOT-P07 and BOOT-P09 were fixed, and not the 7 before BOOT-020. The declared width is derived from the regex it accompanies, so a later widening of one without the other is caught by the differ rather than silently forgiven. KIND MOVED improvement -> additive 2026-09-08 (busbar-oracle v0.3.6): each BOOT-P20/P29/P30 stderr line grew the SAME backtick-quoted expected-one-of list by the four new token-limit metric names, with the surrounding sentence untouched — `text_list_growth` is the kind that proves that byte-for-byte, so this cell is no longer forgiven on the owner's say-so alone but on the tool's own splice check.

accepted.id: F-015 an inline secret is refused without echoing it
accepted.rationale: BOOT-P32 writes an INLINE LITERAL where a secret reference belongs (`providers.gemini.api_key: 7`). 1.5.5 had no scalar visitor on SecretRef, so that value fell through to serde's DEFAULT invalid-type error, which prints the value it was handed: `invalid type: integer `7`, expected a secret reference map: {…}`. The one path this type exists to keep a secret off — stderr and the boot log — is exactly where the rejected secret went, and an unquoted scalar (`api_key: 483920175534`) is the spelling nobody thinks to check. 1.6.0's SecretRef refuses every inline-scalar spelling through one message that states the RULE and never echoes the value: `a secret value must be a REFERENCE, never an inline literal (the value is not echoed): use { env: <VAR> }, { file: <path> }, or { module: <secret-module>, settings: {…} }` (crates/secret-ref/src/lib.rs, RefVisitor::inline_literal). That is the rule the config inventory already documents for every secret-bearing key, so the new sentence tells the operator what to write instead of what serde could not parse. NOT a plane-work side effect: the wording landed on 2026-08-08, long before this branch's base, and reverting it would restore a message that prints an operator's pasted API key into the log. SCOPE: the refusal itself is unchanged — exit code 1, empty stdout, the same `config.yaml: invalid YAML: providers.gemini.api_key: … at line 42 column 14` frame around the sentence, and the same preceding BUSBAR_PROVIDERS deprecation warning byte-for-byte. The `BUSBAR-3015:` prefix on the [error] line is D-1's and is already rewritten away before this entry is consulted. Narrowed to the ONE recorded cell that drives an inline-literal secret; if a fixture ever adds another, name it here explicitly rather than widening the regex to the boot.refusal family.
accepted.changelog: An inline literal where a secret reference belongs is refused without echoing it.

accepted.id: F-013 download error wording

NARROWED 2026-09-05 (the plane-key-lift fix): the two neutrality unknown-key cells dropped — NEUT-U-top's top-level list and NEUT-U-auth's auth: list are byte-identical to 1.5.5 again, because the 1.6.0-additive keys (the plane sections, and auth.policy) are lifted off the document before the frozen 1.5.5-shaped parse. Neither cell has a divergence left to waive. WIDENED 2026-09-05 (A10b): BOOT-W24's `plugins.fetch: miss on reload` warning quotes the SAME reqwest connect-error text change on the SAME download-failure path (`error sending request for url (...)` -> `client error (Connect): tcp connect error: Connection refused (os error 61)`); its `diag=BUSBAR-6001` prefix is D-1 (already covered) and reaches this class only because both fire on the same line.

accepted.id: PR2-D1 degraded non-2xx breaker recording
accepted.changelog: a non-2xx records the breaker outcome by status class, honouring the upstream `Retry-After` as the cooldown floor, and emits the upstream-failure series
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: A non-2xx on a fallback/least-bad/queue hop now records the breaker outcome exactly as the primary hop does (per status class, honouring the upstream Retry-After as the cooldown floor, with the upstream-failure series emitted) instead of a class-less degraded transient with no Retry-After. The client still receives the relayed upstream error; only the breaker bookkeeping and metrics changed.

accepted.id: PR2-D2 degraded hard-down recorded
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: An auth/billing hard-down on a fallback/least-bad/queue hop now trips the lane in every breaker cell and, for busbar's own lane credential, answers with the ingress-native auth-failure envelope — the same rule the primary hop applies. Previously the degraded hop relayed the upstream 401 body verbatim and recorded nothing, leaving the dead lane Closed.
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Improvements: a fallback hop refused upstream is answered in the ingress-native auth-failure envelope and recorded on the breaker

accepted.id: PR2-D3 degraded client-fault counter
accepted.changelog: a client-fault 4xx bumps the lane's `client_fault` counter
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: A client-fault 4xx served through a fallback/least-bad hop now bumps the lane's client_fault observability counter as the primary hop does. No breaker penalty either way; the relayed response is unchanged.

accepted.id: PR2-D4 fallback stream billed
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: OWNER DECISION: bill them. A streaming request served through a fallback/least-bad/queue hop to an OpenAI Chat Completions lane now has stream_options.include_usage injected upstream exactly as a primary hop does, so the trailing usage chunk arrives and the key is billed its real tokens (previously zero). The client-facing stream is unchanged for a client that did not opt in (the injected chunk is stripped at the framing seam); an opted-in client now receives its usage chunk on the fallback hop too. CHANGELOG 1.6.0: 'Fallback-pool and least-bad streams to OpenAI Chat Completions lanes are now metered (previously billed zero tokens).' The egress record shows the injected stream_options.include_usage on the fallback hop.
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Improvements: fallback-lane streams are now billed

accepted.id: PR2-D5 degraded attempt-timeout member override
accepted.changelog: a pool member's `attempt_timeout_ms` override is honoured
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision
accepted.rationale: NAMED GAP, 2026-09-06 (oracle corpus audit): the `cells` regex above names `route.failover|fb|member-slow`, and THAT CELL DOES NOT EXIST. It has never existed -- `git log -S` over enumerate-cells.py finds no revision that defined it, and failover_cells() today yields sixteen `route.failover|*` ids of which none is `fb|member-slow` (the only `slow` cell is `fo|primary-slow`, which drives the PRIMARY pool's lane-level timeout and says so). So this entry matches zero cells and forgives nothing, and unlike M-1, M-2 and S-14 -- each of which states in its own rationale that it deliberately matches nothing today -- it read as though it were scoped. It is not scoped; it is unwitnessed. THE GAP IS TWO THINGS DEEP, which is why it cannot be closed by fixing a regex: oracle-config.sh's `oracle-fb` pool declares one member (`{ model: m-cohere }`) with NO per-member `attempt_timeout_ms` at all, so there is no tighter member override for a cell to observe being honoured. Closing it means a config change (a member override on the fallback pool), a new cell, and a recording from the published 1.5.5 binary -- an owner change with its own harness-revision consequences, not an audit edit. UNTIL THEN, STATED PLAINLY: the behaviour this entry accepts -- a member `attempt_timeout_ms` override taking effect on a fallback or least-bad hop, where the degraded path previously used only the lane-level value -- is UNTESTED by the oracle in either direction. Nothing proves 1.5.5 ignored the override and nothing would catch 1.6.0 applying it wrongly (firing too early on a hop the operator did not tighten, say). The entry accepts only `effects.metrics`, so no money or status class rides on it. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: The pool-member attempt_timeout_ms override is now honoured on fallback/least-bad hops (the degraded path used only the lane-level value). The cap can only fire earlier where an operator set a tighter member override.

accepted.id: PR2-D9 degraded transport-error telemetry
accepted.changelog: a transport error emits the same upstream-failure and failover series
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-04 PR-2 attempt-seam D-table decision

accepted.id: F-011b openapi.json additive endpoints
accepted.changelog: `openapi.json` describes the MCP and A2A endpoints
accepted.rationale: openapi.json adds the mcp/a2a endpoints; every 1.5.5 path and schema is unchanged (a dedicated cell pins info.version). The document also gains a Vary header and reports the binary's true version in info.version (1.5.5 shipped a stale 1.5.4). KIND MOVED improvement -> additive 2026-09-08 (busbar-oracle v0.3.3): the owner ruled on 2026-09-07 that endpoint- and key-list GROWTH is a new feature and not a break, and `additive` makes that ruling machine-checked — the tool proves the candidate document a JSON superset of the 1.5.5 one at every path the golden names, so a 1.5.5 path or schema that CHANGED (rather than one that was added beside it) is still red under this entry. DESCRIPTION_CORRECTIONS ADDED 2026-09-11 (keep-oracle-base-reds): admin.ops|GetOpenapiJson|ok and neutrality|routes|admin-openapi-paths were both still standing RED at `/components/schemas/HookView/description` — commit ee4486486 (the plane-extraction squash) did not just APPEND the `groups`/`phase` paragraph to the struct doc-comment schemars renders here, it also MOVED the existing `groups:`/`phase:` sentence out of its 1.5.5 position mid-paragraph so the new paragraph about the `groups` field's write/read gap could explain both together. The fields themselves (`fires_at`, `groups`, `phase`) are exactly the additive growth this entry's own changelog line already names; the description text was reworded, not merely grown, so `additive_superset`'s plain string-equality check cannot pass it without help. Registered as a correction rather than reverted, since 1.5.5's description is not being restored anywhere else and reverting the doc-comment would put the `groups:`/`phase:` sentence back in a spot that no longer matches how the struct is documented field-by-field. SECOND LEAF ADDED 2026-09-11 (keep-oracle-base-reds): `/components/schemas/HookView/properties/at/description` was still standing RED after the first correction — commit 3c118f729 (which restored the `at` field a clean-slate commit had dropped, "a 1.5.5 client reading this view must see this field byte-for-byte") gave it a new, much longer doc-comment explaining why it is back and why `fires_at` is the field to read instead; 1.5.5's one-line description ("TAP observation stage ..., or `None` for a gate") is superseded by that, not grown beside it. The field's WIRE VALUE is unchanged (still the legacy single-stage string or null) and is not part of this correction. THIRD LEAF ADDED 2026-09-12 (keep-oracle-base-reds): with the first two leaves corrected, the same two cells advanced past `HookView` and stood RED at `/components/schemas/NamedDefView/properties/max_admin_scope/description`. This is not plane-extraction fallout: commit c8780349 (2026-08-08, well before this branch's base) rewrote the field's doc from 1.5.5's "the per-provider ADMIN CEILING (`none` | `read-only` | `full`)" to "(`read-only` | `full`). There is no `none` token: ... a ceiling caps what a grant can reach and cannot express the absence of one", matching that same commit's `Scope::parse_ceiling` refusal message and the dedicated test (admin::tests, PUT identity-providers with `max_admin_scope:"none"` now asserts 400) whose own comment states the reason: 1.5.5 accepted the API write and reported success, but the engine's ceiling parser never accepted `none`, so the config was silently unbootable at the next restart. The wire value is otherwise unchanged (`Option<String>`, omitted when unset); only the description text names the tightened, already-shipped grammar, so `additive_superset`'s plain string-equality check cannot pass it without help. FOURTH AND FIFTH LEAVES ADDED 2026-09-12 (keep-oracle-base-reds), both traced to commit ee4486486 (the same plane-extraction squash as the first leaf) generalizing `OverlaySection::all()`/the overlay-section list from four names to eight: `/components/schemas/NamedDefView/properties/module/description` gained a paragraph explaining `module` is OMITTED (not empty-stringed) for a section with no module, `agents:` being the first such section (`crates/busbar-substrate/src/api.rs`); `/components/schemas/OverlayResetView/properties/reset/description` dropped 1.5.5's hand-written four-name list in favour of pointing at the endpoint's own path-parameter enum, exactly so this class of drift stops recurring every time a section is added (`crates/busbar-core/src/admin/v1/contract/schema.rs`). Neither changes any WIRE behavior 1.5.5 had; both are prose describing the identical additive section-list growth this entry's own changelog line already names. REMAINING LEAVES NOT CORRECTED, LEFT RED ON PURPOSE, ALL UNDER `/paths/...`: the overlay-delete endpoint's `summary` and its `400` response description both interpolate the SAME now-eight-member `overlay_section_names` list (`handlers.rs`/`taxonomy.rs`, built from `OverlaySection::all()`, the same growth as F-011's `/error/message` correction, different location) — but `description_corrections` cannot name either: `resolve_json_pointer` splits a pointer on every `/` with no JSON-Pointer `~1` escaping, so it can never resolve a leaf under a `paths` object, whose own keys (`/api/v1/admin/overlay/{section}`) are themselves full URL paths containing literal `/`. This is a busbar-oracle tool limitation (a separate product, GetBusbar/busbar-oracle), not something this register can work around. The endpoint's `409` response description gained a further, genuinely NEW leading clause, "`conflict`: another config section still references this definition by bare name (remove the reference first)", ahead of 1.5.5's `version_conflict` sentence — a new refusal case (cross-section reference protection on delete), not a reworded existing one. And `/components/schemas/NamedDefView`'s own `required` array independently dropped `module` (schemars marks a `skip_serializing_if`-annotated field optional in the generated schema, and `module` gained that attribute for the same `agents:`-has-no-module reason as the fourth leaf above) — a `required` array SHRINKING is not something `additive_superset`'s list rule or `description_corrections` (string leaves only) can ever pass, by design (see the function's own list-relation docstring: cand must be at least as long as golden). All four remaining leaves are almost certainly intended (the same already-changelogged mcp/a2a-section growth structurally forces `module` optional and drives the two `paths` prose leaves; a delete-time reference guard is a real safety feature), but none has a verbatim CHANGELOG line of its own, and asserting one — or opening a `kind: breaking` sibling entry with a `changelog_reason` — is an owner call this correction does not make unilaterally. Left RED for the owner; see keep-oracle-base-reds' handoff notes for the options (register vs. revert vs. a busbar-oracle upstream fix for the `paths`-pointer limitation). SIXTH LEAF RESOLVED AT THE ROOT 2026-09-12 (OR-BASE-2, on keep-oracle-base-reds): the `required` array's `module` drop (the fifth item above) was struck by measuring 1.5.5's golden (`admin.ops|GetOpenapiJson|ok`), which shows `NamedDefView.module` as `required` and `"type": "string"` (never nullable) for EVERY entry — 1.5.5 had no named-map section whose entries carried no module, so it has no representation for one. `module`'s `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")]` is removed (`crates/busbar-substrate/src/api.rs`); `agents:` entries now serialize `module: ""` instead of omitting the key, `required` is back to `["name", "module", "settings_keys"]` byte-for-byte with 1.5.5, and `openapi.json{,.gz}` are regenerated (`UPDATE_OPENAPI=1`). The FOURTH LEAF's `/components/schemas/NamedDefView/properties/module/description` text changed again (now explains ALWAYS-present/empty-stringed rather than OMITTED) but stays covered by its existing `description_corrections` entry above — the leaf is a prose difference, not a wire one. Only the `/paths/...` leaves (the overlay-delete `summary`/`400`/`409` descriptions) remain RED, for the tool limitation named above.

accepted.id: S-7 responses-door streams stream
accepted.changelog: A `stream: true` request on the Responses door is answered as a stream.
accepted.rationale: A stream: true request on the Responses door is served as text/event-stream with the ResponseStreamEvent sequence; 1.5.5 answered the same-dialect case with a buffered JSON body. Metered identically (250 cents / 18 tokens). The buffered 1.5.5 body carried a synthesized content-length with no transfer-encoding; the SSE body is chunked, so the normalizer's header-shape rule fires where it did not before (norm.rules) -- a byproduct of the same content-type change, not a separate behavior.

accepted.id: E7-1 non-Responses doors stream when the backend is Responses-shaped
accepted.changelog: Every door streams when the routed lane is Responses-shaped.
accepted.rationale: A stream: true request whose routed lane is Responses-shaped is now served as text/event-stream carrying the ingress door's own translated stream frames (Cohere v2 SSE, Gemini's SSE framing, OpenAI chat.completion.chunk SSE); 1.5.5 answered it as a buffered application/json body regardless of the door that received it. The Anthropic- and Bedrock-door cells for the same egress already carry this fix under S-4's and S-1's broader per-door wildcards; this entry covers the three doors (Cohere, Gemini, OpenAI chat) whose own required-member registrations (S-5; none was needed for Cohere/Gemini, which had zero required-member violations) did not include the ok_stream outcome. Metered identically (250 cents / 18 tokens).

accepted.id: S-8 streamed usage carries the same attribution buckets as buffered
accepted.changelog: A streamed response's `usage` carries the same attribution buckets as a buffered one.
accepted.rationale: NARROWED 2026-09-05 (round-3 audit): was `^llm\|[a-z_]+\|[a-z_]+\|request\|ok_stream$`, which forgave a body change on EVERY streamed llm cell (32 of them) when the fix can only move the cells whose upstream actually reports an attribution sub-bucket on the streamed path. In this harness that is exactly the six `<door>|responses` cells: mock-upstream.py's /v1/responses is the only dialect whose usage object carries populated sub-buckets (input_tokens_details.cached_tokens / cache_write_tokens, output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens); anthropic_stream, openai_chat_stream, gemini_stream, cohere_stream and bedrock_stream all send the totals with every sub-bucket null or absent, so no other ok_stream cell has a bucket to gain. `llm|responses|responses|request|ok_stream` is the same-protocol A-tap half of the fix; the other five are the shared trailing-usage fold half. If a fixture ever starts sending sub-buckets on another dialect's stream, add that cell here explicitly rather than restoring the wildcard. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: A stream's usage object now reports every per-dialect attribution sub-bucket the provider sent (reasoning tokens, the two Anthropic cache-creation TTL tiers and its web-search/service-tier pair, the four OpenAI audio and predicted-outputs slices, Gemini's tool-use prompt slice, Cohere's separately-metered billed_units trio), instead of reporting them only when the same request was made with stream:false. 1.5.5 carried NO sub-buckets on either path, so nothing a 1.5.5 client read has changed value or disappeared — the buckets are additive members that were absent before; 1.6.0 recovered them on the buffered path and this closes the streamed half of the same gap, so the two answers for one request finally agree. The totals are untouched: billable_tokens ignores the whole attribution struct. CAVEAT for a future re-record: Cohere's billed_units trio is the one bucket that is NOT a slice of the totals — to_token_usage lets billed_input/billed_output win over the raw counts — so a Cohere backend that reports billed_units on a STREAM will move that stream's ledgered figures to the same numbers its buffered twin already ledgers. No recorded cell exercises it (the oracle mock sends no billed_units on a stream), so this entry accepts `body` only; should a fixture ever start sending it, the effects.usage delta must be re-registered as kind=breaking with a CHANGELOG line rather than folded in here.

accepted.id: M-1 refund reaches the cell the charge reached
accepted.changelog: A failed request's flat fee is refunded even when its window rolled under it.
accepted.rationale: NARROWED 2026-09-05 (round-3 audit): was `^(billing|limits)\|`, which forgave a body or header change on EVERY billing and limits cell — i.e. it would have waived a WRONG BILLING FIGURE in any of those response bodies, the exact class of bug this register exists to surface. The entry's own rationale already states the served change is a no-op on every cell the oracle records (no scripted cell drives a window straddle), so the correct scope is the ONE future cell that will drive it: billing|key-usage|refund-across-window (defined SKIP-able in cells.json; the recorder owes it once the mock can drive a concurrent window roll). Until that cell is recorded this entry matches nothing, which is the point. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: A request pinned to window M whose charge landed in place on a cell a concurrent admission had already rolled to M+1 now has its flat per-request fee refunded from that same cell. 1.5.5 resolved a charge on `window > cell.window_start` (charge in place on a rolled cell) but a refund on `cell.window_start == window`, so the two halves of one request could land on different cells and a failed straddling request kept its fee for the life of that window -- leaving the derived spend a budget cap reads one fee too high. refund_bucket now mirrors resolve_for_charge exactly (`cell.window_start >= window`): the refund reaches the cell the charge reached. A cell genuinely OLDER than the request's window is still a no-op under both rules. Strictly in the client's favour and only ever reachable on a boundary straddle, which no scripted oracle cell drives -- the recorded billing and limits cells are unchanged. The divergence class it WOULD produce is effects.usage, and this register's own rule reserves that class for a kind=breaking entry naming a CHANGELOG line, so if a cell ever does show it the entry must be promoted by the owner rather than widened here.

accepted.id: M-2 a mid-stream upstream failure is not billed as a completion
accepted.changelog: A stream that dies mid-flight is no longer served, and billed, as a completed one.
accepted.rationale: SCOPE IS DEAD AND SAYS SO, 2026-09-06 (oracle corpus audit) -- NOT WIDENED HERE, because widening a register entry is the owner's call and never an auditor's. Two facts about the `cells` regex above, both measured: (a) it names the outcome token `mid-stream-error`, which the enumeration has NEVER produced. enumerate-cells.py's mid-stream failure outcome is spelled `stream_upstream_error` (STREAM_UPSTREAM_ERROR_OUTCOME), so this regex has matched ZERO cells from the moment it was written -- not because the cells are unrecorded, but because no cell has ever borne that id. (b) The round-4 note below says the honest scope is 'the two future cells that will' exercise the shapes, and one of those cells is now PRESENT: the six `llm|<d>|<d>|request|stream_upstream_error` cells exist and carry `mock_control: {"stream-error": true}`, and mock-upstream.py's `openai_chat_stream_error` emits EXACTLY shape (1) -- one good chunk, then `data: {"error":{"type":"server_error",...}}` carrying no `choices`. So the sentence 'the oracle mock has no mock_control verb that injects an inline error chunk' below is out of date for the OpenAI arm; it remains true for shape (2), since `cohere_stream_error` sends an in-band `{"type":"error"}` event and not the terminal `finish_reason: "ERROR"` this entry names. CONSEQUENCE, stated so it cannot be discovered by surprise: those six cells are golden SKIPs today (`needs_fixture`, named gaps on the ledger), so nothing is owed and nothing is forgiven and the register is not currently laundering anything. On the day the integrator records them from the published 1.5.5 binary, `llm|openai|openai|request|stream_upstream_error` will diverge on exactly the frame this entry is about and this entry will NOT cover it -- an UNACCEPTED divergence, i.e. red. That is the fail-closed direction and it is left standing deliberately: the owner rescopes and re-reviews, rather than an audit quietly turning a zero-match entry into a two-match one. NARROWED 2026-09-05 (round-4 audit): was `^llm\|`, which forgave a body change on every one of the 127 recorded LLM cells -- any writer regression whose only symptom is a wrong response body would have reported PASS/ACCEPTED under this entry. The entry's own rationale states no recorded cell exercises either shape, so the honest scope is the two future cells that will (an inline `data: {"error":...}` chunk on an OpenAI-compatible stream, a terminal `finish_reason: "ERROR"` on a Cohere stream); until they are recorded this entry matches nothing. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: Two upstream mid-stream failure shapes were served, and billed, as clean successes. (1) An OpenAI-compatible backend (OpenAI, Azure, vLLM, OpenRouter) that fails AFTER its 200 headers are on the wire delivers the failure inline as a `data: {"error":{...}}` SSE chunk carrying no `choices`; the openai_chat stream reader guarded only on the [DONE] sentinel and `choices`, so the chunk decoded to nothing at all -- no IrStreamEvent::Error, so terminal_error() stayed None, the breaker recorded no fault, the partial completion was billed in full, and a cross-protocol client got balanced block-stops plus an ordinary terminator with no hint the answer was truncated. The gemini, bedrock, anthropic and openai_responses readers each already pushed an Error for their equivalent frame. (2) A Cohere stream ending on the generic infra `finish_reason: "ERROR"` decoded to IrStopReason::Error but pushed no Error event, and no other dialect's writer has a native token for that reason, so every cross-protocol writer rendered it as a success terminator (stop/end_turn) -- the same outcome by a different route. 1.5.5 had the identical gap (v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/proto/openai_chat/reader.rs read_response_events carries the same two guards and no error arm), so this is a deliberate divergence from the pin, named in the 1.6.0 CHANGELOG under Improvements. Strictly in the operator's and the client's favour: a failed request stops being charged for, and a failing lane finally trips. ERROR_TOXIC is deliberately untouched -- it maps to IrStopReason::Safety, a content-moderation refusal is a correctly-served response, and faulting a lane for one would trip the breaker on ordinary safety behaviour. No successful stream changes on any dialect. NO RECORDED CELL EXERCISES EITHER SHAPE: the oracle mock has no mock_control verb that injects an inline error chunk or a terminal ERROR finish_reason (the closest, `cut`, severs the body rather than sending an error frame), so the recorded llm family is unchanged. The divergence classes this WOULD produce on such a cell are `status` and `effects.usage`, and this register's own rule reserves both for a kind=breaking entry naming a CHANGELOG line; this entry therefore accepts `body` only, and if a fixture is ever added that drives one of these shapes the entry must be promoted by the owner rather than widened here.

accepted.id: M-3 Cohere billed_units bill the same buffered and streamed
accepted.rationale: NARROWED 2026-09-06 (shadow-oracle round-5): the `cells` regex was `^llm\|[a-z_]+\|cohere\|request\|ok(_stream)?$|^billing\|`. That trailing `|^billing\|` alternation held this entry's `effects.usage` -- a MONEY class -- over all twelve `billing|*` cells (eleven of them owed), a family this entry's id, rationale and changelog line never mention. Those cells are the ledger's own views (key/group/admin usage, the refund window); a change to what busbar CHARGES, or to what it reports having charged, is precisely the divergence the oracle exists to catch, and it would have reported ACCEPTED under a Cohere waiver. Cohere reaches the billing views only through the same `llm|*|cohere|*` cells already named on the left of the alternation, so the honest scope is exactly those twelve and nothing else; `billing|key-usage|refund-across-window` has its own entry (M-1). The register now requires every entry to declare `expected_cells`, so an alternation bolted onto a live scope stops the run. ORIGINAL RATIONALE: Cohere reports usage TWICE -- a raw `usage.tokens` bucket and a separately-metered `usage.billed_units` bucket -- and billed_units is the count Cohere itself invoices the operator on. 1.5.5 read only `tokens` (its cohere reader parsed usage.tokens on both the stream and the non-stream path; billed_units was never read) and billed those. 1.6.0 lets billed_input_tokens/billed_output_tokens win over the raw totals inside IrUsage::to_token_usage, the one projection the ledger reads. This entry covers the BUFFERED arm finally reaching that same projection: chat_usage (the projection behind ChatRespHandle::billing()) had been rebuilding TokenUsage from the RAW IrUsage totals, so a single completion was billed the billed counts when streamed and the raw counts when buffered -- two different invoices for one completion, decided only by the caller's stream flag. Both arms now answer identically. No other dialect populates the billed fields, so every other backend's ledgered counts stay byte-identical to 1.5.5. The oracle's own mock sends billed_units EQUAL to tokens, so no recorded cell moves today; the entry is registered ahead of any fixture that makes them differ, which is exactly what S-8's caveat requires.
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Improvements: a Cohere backend's `usage.billed_units` is what the key is billed, on both the buffered and the streamed path

accepted.id: F-014 Bedrock totalTokens counts the cache tokens AWS counts
accepted.rationale: AWS Converse reports inputTokens as the NON-cached input only and documents the full input as inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens (its worked caching example totals 16 input + 4 output + 695 cache-write as totalTokens 715). 1.5.5's Bedrock writer derived totalTokens = inputTokens + outputTokens while emitting the two cache counts beside it as ADDITIVE siblings, so on a cache-bearing response the published parts summed PAST the published total and a consumer reading totalTokens -- the field AWS points accounting consumers at -- lost every cache token. Both write sites (the buffered Converse body and the streamed metadata frame) now publish the AWS sum. The component fields are untouched, a response with no cache activity is byte-identical to 1.5.5 (the omitted cache buckets add zero), and this is a Bedrock-INGRESS body shape only: nothing Busbar ledgers reads totalTokens, since the Bedrock reader never parses it. The oracle's mock reports no cache tokens, so no recorded cell moves today.
accepted.changelog: Bedrock `usage.totalTokens` counts the cache tokens AWS counts.

accepted.id: G-1 gemini toolUsePromptTokenCount is an additive term and is billed
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-07 ruling: Gemini billing must be right in 1.6.0
accepted.rationale: MEASURED, NOT READ. Seven real gemini-2.5-flash turns captured off Vertex AI and committed verbatim under crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/tests/proto/golden/vendor/ show usageMetadata.toolUsePromptTokenCount sitting BESIDE promptTokenCount, not inside it: on resp_g2g_vertex_grounding.json the field is 32 while the entire promptTokenCount is 18 -- a slice cannot exceed the total it slices -- and Google's own totalTokenCount (222) reconciles only when the term is ADDED to prompt + candidates + thoughts (190). 1.5.5 documented it as a sub-bucket of the prompt and excluded it from the bill, so every grounded / server-tool Gemini turn was under-counted by exactly that term (32 of 222 tokens, 14%, on that capture) and the shortfall scales with server-side tool use. 1.6.0 bills it in the INPUT tier, where Google charges it: gemini_usage() and GeminiReader::recover_truncated_usage both add it to IrUsage::input_tokens, so a truncated response bills like its buffered twin. The Gemini WRITER is the exact inverse -- the term is subtracted back out of the reconstructed promptTokenCount and added into the synthesized totalTokenCount -- so a native client sees the same wire shape Vertex sends and a totalTokenCount that now reproduces Google's. A turn with no server-side tool use is byte-identical to 1.5.5 and bills identically (the absent term adds zero). NO RECORDED CELL MOVES TODAY: the oracle's mock happy-path answer carries no toolUsePromptTokenCount at all, which is exactly how a 14% under-count survived a full golden, so llm|gemini|gemini|request|ok_tool_use_tokens is added to cells/__init__.py to make the surface visible and is a needs_fixture NAMED GAP until the mock answers the tool-use verb and the integrator records it from the published 1.5.5 binary. WHEN THAT GOLDEN IS RECORDED the new cell will diverge on `body` (the usageMetadata the door re-emits) AND on `effects.usage` (1.5.5 bills 190, 1.6.0 bills 222) -- and this improvement entry may not waive a usage class, so the owner must convert it to kind=breaking, or ratify it as an improvement whose usage divergence is judged on its own row, at that point. Registered now, with the CHANGELOG line, because the money change lands now.
accepted.changelog: A Gemini turn that used a server-side tool bills the tool-use tokens Google charges for.

accepted.id: A17 Anthropic billing_error names its own error type
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-05 oracle Phase 0 group-budget-total cell
accepted.rationale: 1.5.5 answers the group's own BUDGET-total exhaustion (metric: budget, not the requests-cap `over_budget` arm) with error.type "insufficient_quota" — OpenAI's vocabulary, outside the nine types the published Anthropic error envelope declares. 1.6.0 answers the identical 429 with error.type "billing_error", the Anthropic-native member for a billing/quota refusal. Status (429), message text, and every other field are byte-identical on both sides; only /error/type differs: "insufficient_quota" (1.5.5) -> "billing_error" (1.6.0).
accepted.changelog: An Anthropic-dialect error names an Anthropic error type. Busbar's quota and context-overflow refusals reached an Anthropic client as `insufficient_quota` and `context_length_exceeded` — OpenAI's vocabulary, and outside the nine types the published error envelope declares, so the official SDK raised a generic `APIError`. They are now `billing_error` and `invalid_request_error`. The status, message and every other error type are unchanged.

accepted.id: S-9 responses url citations survive the hop
accepted.changelog: **A Responses URL citation survives the hop.**
accepted.rationale: Spec fidelity: the Responses API's published UrlCitationBody FLATTENS url/title/start_index/end_index onto the annotation, while Chat nests them under a url_citation object. 1.5.5 wrote the flat shape but read only the nested one, so every URL citation on a Responses-shaped upstream response was dropped -- including Responses->Responses, where the reader consumed bytes the writer had just produced. 1.6.0 reads both published shapes, so a citation the upstream sent reaches the client. Additive: a response that carried no citation is byte-identical. Owner rule: maximum spec compliance wins over 1.5.5 bytes.

accepted.id: S-10 a cachePoint before a bedrock document does not double the document
accepted.changelog: **A Bedrock `cachePoint` before a document no longer sends the document twice.**
accepted.rationale: Spec fidelity: the Converse reader parks a native document/video block at its WIRE index and also pushes a modelled block into the IR; the writer suppresses the modelled copy when it recognizes the parked one. A cachePoint or guardContent occupies a wire slot but yields no IR block, so past it the wire and IR indices disagree and the suppression missed -- the document was emitted twice, once modelled and once spliced. AWS reads the attachment twice and the caller pays its input tokens twice. 1.6.0 records the two index spaces separately so the block is emitted exactly once. Request-body only; no usage or billing class is waived here -- the double charge is the defect being removed, not an accepted difference.

accepted.id: S-11 a refused responses function-call open emits no output_item.added
accepted.changelog: **A Responses function-call item the writer refused to open no longer announces itself.**
accepted.rationale: Spec fidelity: the Responses stream writer bounds the number of concurrently open function-call items (MAX_OPEN_TOOLS) so a pathological backend cannot grow per-stream state without limit. The cap refused the open but the frame went out anyway: the sibling text and reasoning arms ask their open helper for a verdict and emit nothing when it refuses, while the function-call arm called the helper for its side effect and discarded the answer. Past the cap the wire therefore carried a response.output_item.added for an item that was never tracked -- so its BlockStop found nothing to close, no response.output_item.done ever followed, and the item was absent from the terminal output[] too: a lifecycle open, on the published item union, for an item that never opened and never ends. 1.6.0 decides the frame and the open together. Additive below the cap: a stream with at most MAX_OPEN_TOOLS function-call items is byte-identical. Owner rule: maximum spec compliance wins over 1.5.5 bytes.

accepted.id: S-12 a deferred anthropic redacted_thinking start no longer orphans its stop
accepted.changelog: **An Anthropic `redacted_thinking` block closes only if it opened.**
accepted.rationale: Spec fidelity: the published ContentBlockStartEvent carries a redacted_thinking block's opaque `data` INLINE on the start and declares no delta member for it, so busbar defers that start to the RedactedReasoningDelta that carries the bytes. 1.5.5 marked the index OPEN at the BlockStart -- before the frame existed -- which is the one thing the writer's own orphan-stop guard must not do: the guard's whole job is to suppress a content_block_stop for a block the client never saw opened, and the deferral made it answer for a frame that had not been written. A stream ending between the BlockStart and its delta (a truncation, an upstream error, or the translator draining its own open set) therefore sent a bare content_block_stop -- exactly the orphan close the guard exists to prevent, and outside the spec's 1:1 start/stop pairing. 1.6.0 marks the index open in the code path that WRITES the start, so start and stop are decided by the same fact; the same boolean stops a second redacted delta from writing a duplicate, unpaired start. Byte-identical whenever the delta arrives, which is every non-truncated redacted stream. Owner rule: maximum spec compliance wins over 1.5.5 bytes.

accepted.id: S-13 folded chat usage un-folds without a finish_reason beside it
accepted.changelog: **A streamed chat `usage` trailer arrives even when the stream ended without a stop reason.**
accepted.rationale: Spec fidelity: published include_usage says the token counts ride an ADDITIONAL final chunk whose choices array is always EMPTY. The Chat writer cannot emit two frames for one IR MessageDelta, so it folds the counts onto the chunk it does write and a downstream seam un-folds them into that trailing chunk. The writer folds whenever the terminal counts are nonzero -- NOT only when the delta carries a stop reason -- but both un-fold seams additionally required a non-null finish_reason beside the folded object. A backend that ends a stream with no stop reason (an incomplete Responses stream whose incomplete_details.reason the published spec does not name) produces exactly the chunk neither seam looked at: a client that asked for usage never received it, and a client that opted OUT was sent usage it had not asked for. Both seams now key on the folded object itself, which is only ever present because the writer put it there. Cross-dialect stream bodies only; the same-dialect byte-exact passthrough never reaches these seams, and no usage or billing class is waived -- busbar's own metering reads the IR-side tap upstream of this seam and never moved. Owner rule: maximum spec compliance wins over 1.5.5 bytes.

accepted.id: S-14 a gemini speech response with no audio part is refused, not served as an mp3
accepted.changelog: **A Gemini speech response that carries no audio is no longer served as an MP3.**
accepted.rationale: Spec fidelity: Gemini returns synthesis as JSON with the audio at candidates[0].content.parts[0].inlineData; a mock or a direct passthrough returns the raw audio container instead, so the reader tries JSON and falls back to the bytes. 1.5.5's fallback caught the wrong bodies too: ANY body that parsed as JSON but carried no inlineData -- an error envelope, a SAFETY-blocked candidate, a text-only answer -- was handed back as a 200 whose Content-Type said audio/mpeg and whose bytes were a JSON object. A player could not open it and the upstream's own explanation was unreachable behind an audio label. 1.6.0 refuses a JSON body with no audio part (CodecError::Malformed, which the buffered seam turns into the upstream-shaped error) and leaves the not-JSON-at-all arm exactly as it was, so every real audio container reads byte-identically. This entry matches no cell in today's enumeration -- the llm cells all carry op=chat and no fixture drives the TTS leaf -- and is registered ahead of any speech fixture that would make it visible, the same posture S-8's caveat requires. No status or usage class is waived: the refusal REPLACES a 200 that was already the wrong answer. Owner rule: maximum spec compliance wins over 1.5.5 bytes.

accepted.id: S-15 a duplicate message start keeps the stream id it opened with
accepted.changelog: **One stream states one id.**
accepted.rationale: Spec fidelity: a stream is not guaranteed to carry exactly one IR MessageStart. Five of the six readers gate it on their own started flag, but the Anthropic reader emits it 1:1 with the upstream message_start frame, so ANY egress fed from an Anthropic ingress can see two. 1.5.5's Anthropic, OpenAI-Chat, Gemini and Cohere writers each answered the second one by synthesizing a FRESH id, and the Responses writer latched only its sequence_number reset, not response.id -- so one message announced itself twice under two different identities. Every published streaming contract here fixes the id for the life of the message (a native OpenAI stream repeats ONE id on every chunk; a native Gemini stream's responseId is constant; the Responses SDK reads event.response.id on the terminal event to finalize), and the official SDKs latch the id from the FIRST frame that supplies it -- so the client was left correlating against an id nothing else in the stream ever mentions, and the Responses duplicate additionally disagreed with its own response.completed. 1.6.0 gives each of the five writers a per-stream id cell captured on the opening event and replayed thereafter, carried across a mid-stream Protocol::clone for the same reason the sibling open-block state already is. Byte-identical on every stream with a single opening event, which is every stream from the five gating readers. Stream bodies only; no status or usage class is waived. Owner rule: maximum spec compliance wins over 1.5.5 bytes.

accepted.id: K-1 rotate refuses an overlong key id like its siblings
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Improvements: rotate refuses an overlong key id like its siblings.
accepted.rationale: `reject_overlong_id` is a per-handler call, and `POST /api/v1/admin/keys/{id}/rotate` was the one `/keys/{id}` handler that never made it: read/patch/delete/usage/revoke all answer 400 `invalid_request` / "id must be <= 64 characters", rotate fell through to 404 `not_found` / "key not found". Rotate is also the handler where an unbounded id costs the most -- it is the only one that keys a process-global idempotency cache on the caller's bytes (`rotate:{id}:{k}`), retaining an entry sized by the request for the entry's full TTL -- so the guard sits ahead of the idempotency block rather than beside the governance check. 1.5.5's own contract omitted `Validation / Overlong` from this endpoint's declared error set; declaring it regenerates openapi.json purely additively. REGISTERED `breaking`, NOT `improvement`, because the differ permits only a `breaking` entry with a changelog line to accept the `status` class (diff-cells.py MONEY_CLASSES) -- 404 -> 400 is a status change on a refusal path, and the register's own rule is that no `improvement` may forgive one. In substance this is an improvement: a request that was refused is still refused, with the siblings' code and message instead of a misleading not-found. SCOPE: exactly one cell id. Every other `/keys/{id}` overlong-id cell must stay byte-identical to 1.5.5 -- five handlers that already have the bound may not move, and this entry cannot forgive them if they do.

accepted.id: D-3 money is a lookup over quantities against a dated rate-card history
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Changed: a rate-card edit prices what happens after it, not what happened before it.
accepted.rationale: 1.5.5 stores raw token counts and derives spend_micros AT READ TIME from the CURRENT cost model (crates/busbar-core/src/admin/v1/service.rs:2187, :2230; contract/mod.rs:1077-1079 'MUTABLE ESTIMATE'), so a PUT /config/settings rate_card re-prices every past row with no restart and no epoch boundary. 1.6.0 keeps quantities as the stored truth and keeps deriving the amount at read time, but derives it against the card in force AT THE POSTING'S INSTANT, read from an append-only dated rate-card history (design docs/design/rate-card-history.md §2.3, §9; ARCHITECTURE.md PB-103). A window with no mid-window card change answers BYTE-IDENTICALLY -- a single-entry history effective from instant 0 IS that card, same rates, same order, same saturation, same single truncation -- and a window with one answers with the money each request was actually earned under. SCOPE IS THREE CELL IDS, NAMED IN FULL, NOT A FAMILY PREFIX. They are exactly the recorded cells whose money moves, and each is recorded from the published 1.5.5 binary (the pinned darwin digest) BEFORE the change, so the divergence has a judge that predates it: (1) billing|rate-card|epoch-mid-window -- one mid-window 100x card; a window totalling 10,000,000 micro-units reads back as 1,000,120,000. (2) billing|rate-card|history-mid-window -- TWO cards in one window with /usage read after each; recorded 25,000,000 / 500,060,000 / 750,090,000, i.e. the first request reported at three different prices over the life of one window. Under the history only the LAST read moves (to 277,530,000): the two earlier reads were already the honest figure at their own instant and stay byte-identical, which is why the entry names `body` and `effects.usage` and nothing else. (3) ledger|rate-history|as-of -- GET /admin/usage?as_of=1. 1.5.5 IGNORES the parameter silently, returns the current-card reprice (1,000,120,000) and reports its own as_of as 0, contradicting the URL; 1.6.0 honours it. That is a different number under unchanged request bytes on the legacy endpoint, so it belongs to this breaking entry and not to the additive one, even though the parameter itself is new. The other nine billing| cells and every hazard|, plugins.store-persist| and admin.ops| cell stay IDENTICAL: none edits a card mid-window, so each runs against a single-entry history. ledger|currency|minor-unit-rounding is deliberately OUTSIDE this scope and may not be forgiven by it: it reads /usage under a single-entry sub-cent card (spend_micros 18 per row, 54 as an exact sum, no minor-unit projection anywhere) and must stay byte-identical, which is the identity test's statement 2 stated as a cell. REGISTERED breaking, NOT improvement, because the differ permits only a breaking entry with a changelog line to accept a money class (diff-cells.py MONEY_CLASSES) and spend_micros moving is one. Back-dating is still available and is now attributable: the signed amend-rate-history verb appends a dated entry and emits one journaled, operator-signed repricing record per affected (window, bucket) carrying the old and new card, the quantities, both amounts and the delta, so the original line and the correction are both visible forever and no booked line is rewritten.

accepted.id: D-4 dated rate-card history, native currencies, and the signed amend verb
accepted.changelog: The 1.6.0 ledger endpoints read money as of a rate-card history snapshot.
accepted.rationale: The ADDITIVE half of the rate-card history (design docs/design/rate-card-history.md §11.3): /api/v1/admin/ledger/{rate-history,repricings} are new reads; /api/v1/admin/ledger/amend-rate-history is a new operator-signed write in the irreducible set; the ledger reads gain optional ?as_of=<history_seq> and ?currency=<CCY> and echo history_seq, head, currency and the adjusting entries. A card prices in one or more currencies natively, with no pivot and no conversion. No 1.5.5 path, field or byte is touched: crates/busbar-core/src/admin/v1/json/openapi.json is unchanged and the 1.6.0 operations are described at docs/openapi-1.6.0-additive.json, reached by name at GET /api/v1/admin/ledger/openapi.json. WHAT MAKES THAT CLAIM CHECKABLE RATHER THAN ASSERTED: each cell in scope is recorded from the published 1.5.5 binary (the pinned darwin digest) answering the 1.6.0 call, so 'this surface is new' is a diff and not a belief. ledger|amend|adjusting-entries and ledger|amend|refused-unsigned both record 404 not_found / 'resource not found', BYTE-IDENTICAL to each other -- the router's generic miss, not a 405 from a path that exists for another method -- which is the proof the refusal is about the ROUTE and that 1.5.5 knows nothing about operator signatures. ledger|currency|native records 400 invalid_request, 'unknown field `currency`, expected one of `input_utok`, `output_utok`, `cache_read_utok`, `cache_write_utok`': 1.5.5 REFUSES the per-entry currency key rather than accepting and dropping it, so 1.6.0 honouring it cannot change the meaning of any card an operator can write today. config|rate-card|append-not-replace records the 400 that makes §4.1 well-defined ('rate_card is AUTHORITATIVE and COMPLETE'), including its eight-model remediation block, and STAYS a 400. ledger|currency|minor-unit-rounding is in scope for its /usage shape only and must not move at all: it is a single-entry history and its figures (18 per row, 54 total, no minor-unit projection) are the USD baseline §3.3's per-currency exponent has to leave alone. NO MONEY CLASS IS WAIVED HERE, deliberately. classes is `body`/`headers` only, so this entry cannot forgive a status. The four cells that answer 404/400 today will answer differently once the routes exist, and that status move is NOT accepted by this entry: it is M6's to register when it lands, with its own scope and its own line. Naming the gap is the point -- an acceptance whose scope is 'whatever the new endpoints end up doing' is one nobody can audit.

accepted.id: F-016 a provider api_key that does not resolve refuses boot
accepted.by: owner (Matthew Jackson), 2026-09-07 provider-credential fail-closed decision ("no carve outs, fix it")
accepted.rationale: These two cells exist to pin a WARNING that 1.6.0 deletes. Both drive the same config -- a provider whose api_key names an env var the recorder deliberately does not export -- and 1.5.5 answered it by degrading that provider to an EMPTY key and starting anyway: W16 pins the `provider api_key did not resolve:` warn line, W17 pins the `[warn] provider gemini api_key (env:...) empty` line that the degrade's String::new() then trips. Both recorded exit 0 and a serving gateway. The provider credential was the one secret in busbar that was not fail-closed, and the lane the degrade produced could not work: it reported healthy, the health prober skipped it (no key, no probe), and every request routed to it came back 401 from the upstream, with one boot warning as the only signal. 1.6.0 refuses instead, under BUSBAR-8020, naming the provider and the reference (`env:VAR`, `file:/path`) and never the value -- the same answer `busbar --validate` has given since 1.5.3, so boot and validate now agree. That moves all three recorded classes on both cells: status 0 -> 1, the boot log body (the WARN line is gone), and stderr (the degrade's `[warn] ... empty` line is gone, and the boot stops before the model/pool summary). status is a MONEY class, so this is registered as kind=breaking with its CHANGELOG line rather than as an improvement. An upstream that genuinely takes no credential is no longer inferred from a failure to read one: it is DECLARED with the new `api_key: none` scalar, which starts the lane, sends no auth header and is skipped by the prober -- covered going forward by the new boot.refusal|BOOT-152b|boot cell (the refusal, the boot-mode twin of the --validate-only BOOT-152) and by unit/CLI tests for the declaration. Scoped to exactly the two recorded cells whose expected output IS the deleted warning; every other boot.warning cell is untouched. WIDENED 2026-09-07 to boot.refusal|BOOT-P31|validate (class effects.stderr only): the inline-literal refusal's sentence now lists the bare scalar `none` as the fourth accepted form of a provider api_key, because that is the only spelling of a keyless upstream once the degrade path is gone; the status, the exit code and the refusal itself are unchanged.
accepted.changelog: 1.6.0 Breaking: a provider whose `api_key` reference does not resolve now refuses boot; keyless local upstreams must declare `api_key: none`.
